Jenna (ACME SRE): Hey team, ACME dedicated pool eu-west-1-prod-2 showing repeated 429s and 95th latency jumps since ~08:10 UTC. Only started after the autoscaler policy change this morning. :frowning:
Priya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Jenna. Can you share a short sample of error responses and the pool id? We can start with node list + MIG partitions.
Jenna (ACME SRE): Pool id: rdw-dedicated-eu2-347. Sample error from app logs: `upstream: 429 throttled by serving-runtime (quota exceeded)`; we also see `inference_latency_ms p95=1120` vs normal ~180.
Sam (Oncall Eng): @Priya I'll pull the pool allocation. Priya, did ACME recently change burst or reserved % in their Dedicated config?
Priya (Support): Checking their config now — policy shows reserved_capacity=80% and burst_limit=20% unchanged. Autoscaler rule was tweaked to reduce scale-up aggressiveness at 4:30am UTC -> could be delaying new node adds.
Alex (Infra): Could also be noisy neighbor on MIG slices. Jenna, can you run `rdwctl node list --pool rdw-dedicated-eu2-347` and paste node ids + GPUs? If you can't, we'll fetch from control plane.
Jenna (ACME SRE): Pasting output (redacted):
```
node-10-4a (10.4.1.12) : 4xA100 (MIG 1g.10g, 1g.5g, 1g.5g, 1g.1g)
node-10-4b (10.4.1.13) : 4xA100 (MIG 1g.10g, 1g.10g, 1g.5g, 1g.1g)
node-10-4c (10.4.1.14) : 4xA100 (no MIG - whole GPU allocated)
```
Priya (Support): Interesting — one node has whole-GPU allocations mixed with MIG nodes. That can cause scheduling pressure if runtime tries to pack small jobs onto MIG-sliced GPUs and big jobs onto whole GPUs. Any recent model changes that switch from small to large batch sizes?
Jenna (ACME SRE): We rolled a model update 07:50 that increased max_batch_tokens for chat-model from 1024 -> 4096. Could be larger requests now.
Sam (Oncall Eng): That explains it. Larger requests need whole-GPU capacity; autoscaler slowed scale-ups; meanwhile small single-G MIG slices are getting saturated with other tenants. We need quick mitigation: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens to previous value; 2) if unable, we can evict/cordon node-10-4c to avoid mixed packing; 3) increase burst capacity for this pool.
Priya (Support): Agreed. Jenna — can you revert the model config to 1024 for now and confirm if errors stop? If you need us to take node out of rotation, reply and we'll coordinate.
Jenna (ACME SRE): Rolling batch token revert now. Will monitor.
(deploy-bot): Jenna started deployment rdw-models/chat-v12 -> rdw-dedicated-eu2-347 at 08:38 UTC
Jenna (ACME SRE): Revert done. Early telemetry: p95 dropped to ~240ms, 429s stopped. Still seeing occasional spikes when large requests run.
Alex (Infra): For long-term: we recommend aligning MIG partitioning across the pool (avoid mixing whole-G and MIG on same pool) or use allocation classes so large models land on whole-G nodes. We can also tweak scheduler to prefer whole-G for requests with token_count > 2048.
Priya (Support): Filed internal ticket INFRA-1298 to standardize partitions for ACME pool and add scheduler rule. Action items: Priya to coordinate node remediation, Alex to propose MIG layout, Sam to monitor autoscaler tune, Jenna to validate after next deploy.
Jenna (ACME SRE): Thanks all — please escalate if autoscaler changes are required. We'll keep an eye and report back if anything recurs. :thumbsup:
Priya (Support): Thanks @Jenna. Closing this thread after follow-up ticket. :eyes:
